a) Scientific Claims and Findings
The authors present GlobalTomo, the first large-scale, 3D global synthetic dataset tailored for seismic wavefield modeling and full-waveform inversion (FWI). Their approach integrates acoustic and elastic wave physics, spherical harmonics parameterization, and full 3D wavefields. The dataset is generated using the AxiSEM3D solver and structured into three tiers of complexity: Acoustic, Elastic, and Real Earth.
The authors make 4 key claims:
•	ML models can significantly accelerate seismic forward modeling and inversion.
•	The dataset enables benchmarking of both physics-informed and conventional ML methods.
•	Robustness experiments show resilience to real-world imperfections like noise and missing data.
•	The dataset and code are publicly available and well-documented, promoting reproducibility.
 
b) Strengths of the Paper (Aligned with DB Track CFP)
•	Novelty and Scope: First benchmark dataset at global scale for seismic modeling, bridging geophysics and ML.
•	Technical Rigor: Incorporates realistic wave physics and spherical harmonics parameterization.
•	Comprehensive Benchmarking: Evaluates multiple ML models across forward and inverse tasks.
•	Reproducibility: Dataset and code are openly available on Hugging Face and GitHub, with detailed documentation and scripts 
•	Robustness: Demonstrates model stability under noise and missing data conditions 
•	Clarity and Presentation: Well-structured paper with informative figures and tables.
•	Community Impact: Addresses a long-standing bottleneck in global FWI and provides a foundation for future research.
 
c) Weaknesses and Missing Elements (Relative to DB Track CFP)
•	Synthetic Nature of Data: Dataset lacks real-world seismic data, limiting direct applicability to operational pipelines 
•	Real Earth Tier Evaluation: Benchmarks for the most realistic tier are not yet included, though planned 
•	Uncertainty Quantification: No current integration of Bayesian or ensemble methods to assess inversion confidence 
•	Domain Generality: Some reviewers questioned whether seismology presents uniquely challenging problems compared to other PDE systems 
 
d) Justification for Recommendation: Accept (Poster)
This submission is a technically solid and impactful contribution to the ML-for-science community, particularly in geophysics. It aligns well with the DB Track CFP by:
•	Delivering a high-quality, reproducible dataset that enables rigorous benchmarking of ML models for physics-based tasks.
•	Addressing real-world challenges in seismic modeling through robustness experiments and extensible architecture.
•	Demonstrating community value through open access, clarity, and thoughtful engagement with reviewer feedback.
While not suited for spotlight/oral due to the absence of real-world data and Real Earth tier benchmarks, its foundational nature and broad utility justify acceptance as a poster.
 
e) Reviewer Discussion and Rebuttal Summary
Reviewer SoFY:
•	Concerned about lack of real-world imperfections.
•	Authors added robustness experiments with noise and missing data.
•	Reviewer maintained acceptance rating.
Reviewer 2RoK:
•	Strong accept based on novelty, benchmarking, and reproducibility.
•	Rebuttal clarified dataset realism, future plans for Real Earth tier, and robustness.
•	Reviewer maintained strong accept.
Reviewer AGtw:
•	Borderline accept due to perceived lack of uniqueness and generality.
•	Authors clarified distinctions from existing datasets and seismology-specific challenges.
•	Reviewer remained unconvinced and kept original rating.
Reviewer wmzr:
•	Accepted after rebuttal addressed concerns about Real Earth tier, speed-accuracy trade-offs, and spatial analysis.
•	Authors added geographic performance breakdown and committed to future benchmarks.
 
Final Recommendation: Accept (Poster)
Despite some reservations from one reviewer, the consensus is that the paper presents a technically rigorous, well-documented, and highly accessible benchmark dataset that fills a critical gap in seismic ML research. The authors have shown strong engagement during the rebuttal and demonstrated a clear pathway to future improvements.

We thank the reviewer AGtw for the follow-up and for sharing these continued concerns. We address each point below in the same order.
> Benefits over regional Cartesian-based datasets

 The main motivation for adopting different numerical approaches lies in their distinct speed–accuracy trade-offs and their ability to model global-scale geometries with high fidelity. As shown in the foundational AxiSEM3D work [1], traditional numerical methods exhibit fundamental trade-offs:

 * Finite Element Methods: Highly accurate but computationally prohibitive at global scales.
 * Finite Difference Methods: Highly efficient (10–100× faster than finite elements) but suffer from 10–20% accuracy loss in complex geometries.
 * Spectral Element Methods (AxiSEM3D): Achieve 2–3 orders of magnitude speedup over full 3D finite elements with <1% accuracy loss, while handling global curvature and structural complexity.

These differences are not cosmetic—they fundamentally change the feasible simulation scope, resolution, and resource requirements, which in turn influence the quality and usability of the dataset. In conclusion, we chose AxiSEM3D for its efficient simulation of global-scale seismology data.

> Simulation vs. real-world validation

 We agree that validation on real-world data is essential. As a first step, we follow the practice of many baseline datasets by starting with clean, controlled simulation data to ensure reproducibility and isolatable benchmarking. We have also included experiments with noisy synthetic data to emulate more realistic conditions (please see our response to Reviewer 2RoK). In future work, we plan to extend the dataset with forward modeling and inversion on real seismic data, enabling direct real-world validation.

> Added value of pure 3D wavefields

 Pure 3D wavefields are valuable not only as an independent research target in forward modeling but also as a tool for improving inversion workflows:

 * Interpretability: They provide rich **physical traces for interpretability** linking velocity structures to observable seismograms, aiding physical understanding.
 * Flexibility in inversion: They can serve as a form of **physics-based regularization**, helping alleviate ill-posedness.
 Please see our detailed discussion in Appendix G.2.

> Uniqueness of seismology’s computational challenges

 We fully acknowledge that many PDE systems are equally or more complex than seismic wave propagation. Our focus here is not to claim exclusivity in complexity, but to provide a comprehensive, standardized dataset for a specific and important application domain—geophysical forward modeling and full-waveform inversion. By establishing a high-quality benchmark in this domain, we hope to **complement, not compete with**, other PDE-focused datasets and pave the way for broader cross-domain exploration in the future.

[1] Leng, K., Nissen-Meyer, T., Van Driel, M., et al. AxiSEM3D: broad-band seismic wavefields in 3-D global earth models with undulating discontinuities. Geophysical Journal International, 2019.

We hope that our further responses can address your concerns regarding the rationale for using AxiSEM3D to generate the dataset, its potential application to real experiments, the value of simulating full 3D wavefields, and the distinct challenges posed by seismology. Thank you again for your constructive feedback and continued support! We are glad to provide additional clarifications should the reviewer have further questions.

I would like to thank the reviewers for their detailed rebuttal.  However, my main concerns remain unresolved. More specifically:
1. I am not convinced of the benefits of using requiring fundamentally different numerical approaches bring compared to regional Cartesian-based datasets. Do these numerical approaches yield higher accuracies? Ultimately, both are simulation results without validation against real experiments. Therefore, I do not see the added value of including pure 3D wavefields generated solely by simulation.
2. Also, I remain unconvinced that seismology presents uniquely challenging computational or methodological problems. There are other PDE systems that are considerably more complex.

As a summary, given the existence of many seismology-related datasets, I am not inclined to increase my rating.

rebuttal.value:
We extend our sincere gratitude to the reviewer for recognizing GlobalTomo as a pioneering contribution to ML-enabled geophysical science. We are particularly pleased by your acknowledgment of the dataset's high fidelity, comprehensive benchmarking approach, and exceptional reproducibility standards. Your constructive feedback provides valuable guidance for strengthening both the current work and future developments. 

> Real Earth Tier Benchmarking 

We acknowledge the reviewer's important observation regarding the absence of comprehensive benchmarks for our most realistic tier. This limitation reflects both computational constraints and the substantial methodological complexity introduced by fully coupled acoustic-elastic wave propagation in realistic Earth models. 

**Current Research Initiatives:**

We are actively conducting extensive experiments on Real Earth tier inversion, focusing on several advanced methodological approaches. These comprehensive Real Earth tier results will be incorporated in our future work and made available as extended benchmarks to the community. The computational demands of this tier require careful optimization, but we anticipate releasing initial results within the next few weeks.

> Speed-Accuracy Trade-offs in Traditional Numerical Methods 

**Traditional Method Landscape:**

As extensively analyzed in the foundational AxiSEM3D literature [1], traditional numerical methods exhibit fundamental trade-offs:

- Finite Difference Methods: Computationally efficient but limited accuracy for complex geometries (typical speedup: 10-100x, accuracy loss: 10-20%)

- Finite Element Methods: High accuracy but computationally prohibitive for global scales (baseline accuracy, computational cost: reference)

- Spectral Element Methods (AxiSEM3D): Optimal balance achieving 2-3 orders of magnitude speedup with <1% accuracy loss compared to full 3D finite elements

Additionally, the AxiSEM3D literature provides an analysis across different mesh resolutions in Figure 9, demonstrating that the acceleration benefits are more pronounced at finer resolutions. We will incorporate a summary of these findings in our revised manuscript.

**ML Method Positioning:**

Our ML approaches achieve an additional 3-4 orders of magnitude acceleration beyond optimized spectral element methods, enabling real-time global wavefield computation while maintaining correlation >80% with high-fidelity simulations. This represents a qualitatively different computational regime that enables previously intractable applications such as real-time earthquake monitoring and probabilistic hazard assessment.

[1] Leng, K., Nissen-Meyer, T., Van Driel, M., et al. AxiSEM3D: broad-band seismic wavefields in 3-D global earth models with undulating discontinuities. *Geophysical Journal International*, 2019.

> Addressing the Synthetic-to-Real Data Gap

We acknowledge the fundamental challenge of synthetic-to-real transferability in computational geophysics. To systematically evaluate practical applicability, we conducted robustness analyses simulating key sources of real-world uncertainty.

| Imperfection Type | Severity | Correlation (r) | 
|-------------------|----------|-----------------| 
| Missing Data | 0% | 0.826 ± 0.039 | 
| | 5% | 0.809 ± 0.041 | 
| | 10% | 0.788 ± 0.042 | 
| | 15% | 0.762 ± 0.044 | 
| | 20% | 0.731 ± 0.047 | 
| Gaussian Noise | 0% | 0.826 ± 0.039 | 
| | 1% | 0.817 ± 0.039 | 
| | 2% | 0.791 ± 0.037 | 
| | 3% | 0.753 ± 0.036 | 
| | 4% | 0.708 ± 0.036 | 

The results demonstrate remarkable resilience, with the InversionMLP maintaining >70% of baseline performance even under severe imperfections (20% missing data or 4% noise). This suggests promising transferability to real-world scenarios, though we acknowledge that comprehensive validation on observational data remains essential.

> Spatially Resolved Performance Analysis

Following the reviewer's valuable suggestion, we conducted detailed geographic analysis of inversion performance to identify potential regional biases and inform targeted improvements.

**Latitude-Dependent Performance Evaluation:**

| Latitude Range | Geographic Region | Correlation (r) | 
|----------------|-------------------|-----------------| 
| (-10°, 10°) | Equatorial | 0.841 ± 0.074 |
| (10°, 30°) | Tropical | 0.841 ± 0.062 |
| (30°, 50°) | Mid-Latitude | 0.830 ± 0.069 |
| (50°, 70°) | High-Latitude | 0.800 ± 0.133 |
| (70°, 90°) | Polar | 0.727 ± 0.269 |

**Geographic Performance Insights:**

The analysis reveals systematic performance degradation toward polar regions, with several potential contributing factors:

1. Geometric Distortion: Spherical coordinate singularities at poles may introduce numerical artifacts
2. Wave Complexity: Enhanced multipathing and focusing effects in polar geometries
3. Physical Anisotropy: Stronger anisotropic effects in polar regions not fully captured in our parameterization

This geographic analysis provides crucial guidance for targeted improvements, including polar-specific data augmentation and geometric regularization strategies.

> Responses to Specific Technical Questions

**Dataset Generation Code Availability:**

We appreciate this practical suggestion and will incorporate comprehensive AxiSEM3D generation scripts in our public repository. These will include:

- Parameter configuration templates for each dataset tier
- Automated workflow scripts for large-scale generation
- Performance optimization guidelines for different HPC environments
- Quality control and validation procedures

This addition will significantly enhance reproducibility and enable community extensions of the dataset.

**Noise Robustness Assessment:**

As detailed in our synthetic-to-real gap analysis above, the InversionMLP demonstrates considerable robustness to input noise, maintaining >70% of baseline performance even under 4% Gaussian noise conditions. 

**Mathematical Notation Clarification:**

The colon notation in Equation (A3) represents the tensor double contraction (inner product), equivalent to the Frobenius inner product for matrices. We will clarify this notation in our revision to enhance mathematical clarity.

**Conclusion**

We are grateful for the reviewer's thorough evaluation and constructive suggestions. We respectfully acknowledge the reviewer's concern regarding potential overlap with existing datasets. However, we believe there may be some factual misunderstanding about the fundamental differences between GlobalTomo and prior works that we would like to clarify systematically.

**Comprehensive Comparative Analysis:** 

| Dataset | Scale | Wave Types | Data Types | Structural Variability | Parameterization |
|---------|-------|------------|------------|----------------------|------------------|
| OpenFWI | Regional (2D/small 3D) | Acoustic | Seismograms only | Mesh-based perturbations | Grid-based |

**Critical Distinctions:**

1. Scale and Geometry: GlobalTomo uniquely addresses global-scale problems with spherical geometry, requiring fundamentally different numerical approaches (spectral element methods with azimuthal expansion) compared to regional Cartesian-based datasets.

2. Comprehensive Data Modalities: Unlike existing datasets that provide only surface recordings, GlobalTomo includes full 3D wavefields, enabling research on:

- Physics-informed learning with interior field constraints
- Multi-scale feature extraction from wave propagation patterns
- Intermediate representation learning for inverse problems

3. Systematic Structural Parameterization: Our spherical harmonics parameterization (up to degree 8) provides geophysically meaningful structural variations, contrasting with ad-hoc mesh perturbations in regional datasets.

**Scientific Impact and Community Need:**

The global seismology community has long sought ML-accelerated solutions for Earth-scale tomography, a problem fundamentally different from regional exploration geophysics addressed by existing datasets. Our dataset fills this critical gap, enabling research on planetary-scale inverse problems that are computationally intractable with traditional methods.

We appreciate the reviewer's thoughtful observation about the potential generalizability of our benchmarking approach to other PDE systems. This perspective highlights both the broader impact and specific value of our contribution.

**Seismology-Specific Technical Challenges:**

While the general framework could indeed be adapted to other domains, seismology presents unique computational and methodological challenges that distinguish our contribution:

1. Multi-Scale Spherical Geometry: Global wave propagation requires handling wavelengths spanning 6+ orders of magnitude (local to planetary scales) within curved geometry

2. Discontinuous Media: Sharp velocity contrasts at Earth's discontinuities (crust-mantle, core-mantle boundaries) create complex wave interactions rarely encountered in other PDE applications

3. Multi-Modal Wave Physics: Simultaneous P/S wave propagation with mode conversions represents coupled hyperbolic systems of exceptional complexity

4. Ill-Posed Inverse Problems: Global tomography exhibits extreme non-uniqueness requiring specialized regularization and uncertainty quantification approaches

Rather than limiting our contribution to domain-specific benchmarking, GlobalTomo in turn also would serve as a comprehensive testbed for several fundamental ML-for-science methodologies:

- Neural Operator Learning: Testing scalability and generalization across extreme parameter ranges
- Physics-Informed Methods: Validating constraint enforcement in multi-physics coupled systems  
- Inverse Problem Solving: Benchmarking direct vs. optimization-based inversion strategies
- Multi-Scale Learning: Evaluating hierarchical approaches for planetary-scale problems

**Robustness Validation Under Real-World Conditions:**

To systematically evaluate the practical applicability of our approach, we conducted comprehensive robustness experiments simulating two critical sources of real-world uncertainty prevalent in seismic tomography:

1. **Data Incompleteness**: Modeling station failures, transmission losses, and equipment malfunctions through systematic data removal (5-20%)

The results demonstrate remarkable resilience, with the InversionMLP maintaining >70% of baseline performance even under severe imperfections (20% missing data or 4% noise). We appreciate the reviewer's recognition of the substantial computational investment required for dataset generation. The 100,000+ CPU hours reflect the inherent complexity of global-scale seismic wavefield simulation, which demands fine spatiotemporal discretization to accurately capture multi-scale wave propagation phenomena.

**Optimization Strategies Employed:**

- Advanced Simulation Framework: We leveraged AxiSEM3D [1], which achieves 2-3 orders of magnitude speedup over conventional 3D finite element methods while maintaining high physical fidelity

- Efficient Parameterization: Spherical harmonics representation (degree ≤8) reduces computational complexity while capturing geophysically relevant heterogeneity

- Optimized Azimuthal Expansion: Fourier domain calculations significantly reduce memory requirements and computational overhead

**Community Impact and Accessibility:**

While the initial generation cost is substantial, the resulting dataset eliminates this barrier for the broader research community. Individual forward simulations that previously required hours can now be performed in milliseconds, democratizing access to global-scale seismic modeling capabilities.

> Uncertainty Quantification Framework

The reviewer correctly identifies uncertainty quantification as a critical component for robust geophysical inversion. Our current benchmarking focused on establishing baseline accuracy and generalization capabilities across diverse ML architectures.

**Future UQ Integration:**

Our dataset architecture is fully compatible with probabilistic ML frameworks, including:

- Bayesian Neural Networks: For epistemic uncertainty estimation
- Ensemble Methods: For aleatoric uncertainty characterization  
- Variational Inference: For efficient approximate posterior sampling
- Monte Carlo Dropout: For practical uncertainty quantification during inference

We are actively developing comprehensive UQ benchmarks and will incorporate these analyses in future releases, positioning GlobalTomo as a testbed for probabilistic inversion methodologies.

We acknowledge that the absence of Real Earth tier inversion results represents a limitation in our current evaluation. This omission was primarily due to computational constraints and space limitations in the initial submission.

**Ongoing Research Initiatives:**

We are currently conducting extensive experiments on Real Earth tier inversion, focusing on:

- Hybrid Inversion Strategies: Combining physics-informed constraints with data-driven priors
- Multi-Scale Approaches: Leveraging hierarchical model structures for global-to-regional inversion
- Comparative Analysis: Benchmarking against traditional adjoint-based methods

These results will be included in our future work.

The reviewer's observation regarding DeepONet's temporal extrapolation limitations (Figure 3c) highlights a fundamental challenge in neural operator learning for time-dependent PDEs.

summary.value: This paper introduces GlobalTomo, the first comprehensive 3D global synthetic dataset designed for seismic wavefield modeling and full-waveform inversion (FWI) using machine learning. It integrates acoustic and elastic wave simulations across three tiers of complexity, from simplified fluid models to realistic Earth-scale structures. The dataset is generated using the AxiSEM3D solver and supports both data-driven and physics-informed ML approaches. The authors benchmark several neural operators and inversion strategies to demonstrate the dataset’s utility for fast and accurate global seismic modeling.

strengths_contributions.value:
- Significant Contribution:
The dataset addresses a long-standing bottleneck in global FWI by providing a scalable, high-quality benchmark dataset that bridges geophysical modeling and ML-based inversion, a notable gap in the literature.
- Novelty:
Unlike prior FWI datasets (e.g., OpenFWI), which focus on regional or shallow exploration, GlobalTomo scales up to full Earth models with varying wave physics and realistic parameterization. The use of spherical harmonics up to degree 8 is both physically grounded and computationally efficient (Section 2.2).
- Diverse ML Baselines and Evaluation:
The paper provides a rigorous empirical benchmark using MLP, DeepONet, H-Fourier, GNOT, and PIDO across both acoustic and elastic tiers (Section 3.1–3.2). Performance is evaluated on generalization to unseen velocity models and higher-resolution time domains, with meaningful metrics (RL2, Pearson R) and qualitative plots (Figure 2, 3a-c).
- Inversion Analysis:
The paper explores both optimization-based and direct inversion (e.g., InversionNet-3D and InversionMLP), and shows that direct mapping models significantly outperform optimization-based ones in accuracy and efficiency (Table 3, Figure 6).
- Public Availability and Reproducibility:
The dataset and code are openly available (https://global-tomo.github.io), and Appendix F details the training setup. This transparency is commendable and supports community adoption.
- Well-Presented:
The paper is clearly structured and easy to follow. Figures like the overview (Figure 1), architecture comparisons, and inversion visualizations are informative and visually effective. Section 3.2.3 also reflects on the dataset’s uniqueness, practical limitations, and societal impact.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
- Real-World Data Gap:
The dataset is purely synthetic. While the authors argue for its realism via spherical harmonic perturbations and PREM-based structure, there’s still an absence of real Earth noise, station coverage irregularities, or data artifacts that affect real FWI performance (Section 3.2.3). This limits the model’s direct transferability.
- High Computational Cost for Dataset Generation:
Despite improvements in ML inference speed, dataset generation required over 100,000 CPU hours (Section 2.3). This could be a barrier for those wishing to replicate or extend the dataset without access to substantial computing resources.
- Lack of Uncertainty Quantification:
While models are benchmarked for accuracy, there is no discussion of uncertainty quantification in ML predictions or inversions. Given the ill-posedness of FWI, uncertainty estimates (e.g., via Bayesian ML or ensembles) would enhance scientific rigor and interpretability.
- Limited Inversion Evaluation for Real Earth Tier:
Although the dataset includes a Real Earth tier, inversion evaluations are only shown on acoustic data from the simpler tiers. It would strengthen the paper to include inversion results or challenges for the most realistic tier.
- Temporal Generalization Challenges:
Figure 3c shows that DeepONet struggles to generalize to unseen time steps without additional constraints. While physics-informed methods mitigate this, it suggests limited extrapolation capacity in standard ML baselines.

The submission provides a new dataset—GlobalTomo—along with accompanying code and baseline models. According to the paper and Appendix A, the dataset and code are publicly accessible at:

🌐 https://global-tomo.github.io

The dataset is:
- Provided in its final form, covering three tiers (Acoustic, Elastic, and Real Earth).
- Well-documented, with details on simulation parameters, file structure, and usage guidance.
- Designed to be immediately usable by the machine learning and geophysics communities.

Baseline models and scripts for reproducibility and benchmarking are also included. These resources are offered in executable formats and support both forward modeling and inversion workflows.

Thus, the submission fully meets the requirements for dataset and benchmark accessibility.

final_justification.value:
I recommend 6: Strong Accept, based on the following points:
1. Key Issues Resolved in Rebuttal
- The authors clarified the realism of the dataset’s Earth-scale tier, including its parameterization and motivation for omitting real seismic noise in the current release.
- They confirmed that the dataset is intended as a benchmark for both physics-based and ML-based approaches, with real-data integration planned for follow-up work.
- Concerns about reproducibility were fully addressed by demonstrating that the dataset, simulation code, and baselines are publicly available in executable form.
2. Strengths Maintained
- Novelty & Impact: First large-scale, 3D global seismic dataset integrating acoustic and elastic simulations with realistic spherical harmonics parameterization, filling a gap between regional FWI datasets and full Earth-scale modeling.
- Comprehensive Benchmarking: Rigorous evaluation across multiple neural operators and inversion strategies, with clear metrics and visualizations, enabling fair and replicable comparisons.
- Accessibility: Fully documented dataset, code, and scripts promote adoption in both geophysics and ML communities.
- Clarity: The paper is well-organized with informative figures (e.g., dataset overview, inversion examples) and an explicit discussion of limitations and societal impacts.
3. Remaining Minor Limitations
- The dataset lacks real-world noise and irregular station coverage, limiting direct deployment to operational FWI pipelines.
- Uncertainty quantification in inversion outputs is absent but acknowledged as future work.
- Inversion experiments on the most realistic tier are not yet included.

Given the technical rigor, community value, and clear reproducibility, the contributions substantially outweigh these remaining limitations.

summary.value: This paper presents GlobalTomo, a large-scale and comprehensive 3D global synthetic dataset designed for physics-informed machine learning research in seismic wavefield modeling and full-waveform inversion (FWI). The dataset has three degrees of complexity, simulating both acoustic and elastic wave propagation at near global scales. The authors benchmark several machine learning baselines on both forward modeling and inversion tasks to enhance the understanding of the earth's interior with physics-ML modeling.

strengths_contributions.value:
1. **Well-written**: The paper is well-organized and easy to follow. It provides thorough experimental analysis and detailed explanations.

2. **Large-scale**: The dataset simulates global-scale wave propagation using physically meaningful governing equations and realistic structural parameterizations, aiming toward real-earth applications.

3. **Benchmarking with various ML models**: The authors provide extensive ML baselines and discuss both forward modeling and inversion, which is valuable for the seismic ML community.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
1. **Limited uniqueness compared to existing works**: As shown in Table A1, while the dataset is large-scale, similar efforts such as OpenFWI and SeisBench already exist, some of which also support global-scale or different wave-type simulations. SeisBench, in particular, includes global-scale data. Additionally, both wave-type simulations and wavefield information are available from previous datasets. Therefore, the distinctiveness of GlobalTomo is somewhat reduced.

2. **Domain- and PDE-specific benchmarking limits its impact**: The dataset is entirely generated by simulation under a chosen set of governing equations (acoustic/elastic wave equations, etc.) and some pre-determined boundary conditions. While this controlled setup is valuable for evaluating physics-ML models on forward simulation and inversion, it also means that the work essentially amounts to "benchmarking physics-ML methods on one particular PDE system." The same approach could be ported to entirely different domains—e.g., Navier–Stokes for fluid mechanics with certain boundary conditions—so the core methodological contribution is not unique to seismology. As a result, the benchmark’s relevance to the wider scientific-computing or ML-for-science communities may be modest.

ethical_considerations.value: No, there are no or only very minor ethics concerns

dataset_code_comments.value: The dataset can be found in the Github repository. The authors provide details for reproducing the final results.

final_justification.value:
As mentioned in my response to the rebuttal, my concerns regarding the following aspects remain:
1. All of the data is generated by simulation and not validated (I believe that it cannot be validated) against real experiments. 
2. Also, I remain unconvinced that seismology presents uniquely challenging computational or methodological problems. There are other PDE systems that are way more complex.

Given the existence of many seismology-related datasets, I am keeping the original rating.

summary.value: This paper introduces GlobalTomo, a novel 3D synthetic dataset designed for global seismic tomography. The authors present preliminary benchmarks using several existing machine learning models. The dataset is structured into three tiers of increasing complexity: Acoustic, Elastic, and Real Earth. The paper demonstrates that by using this dataset, the forward modeling of seismic waves can be significantly accelerated, and various strategies for the inverse problem (inversion) can be explored.

strengths_contributions.value:
* The dataset is a pioneering contribution to the field of Machine Learning for geophysical science, providing a foundational benchmark for tackling large-scale problems.
* The dataset comprehensively covers three distinct scales of complexity. The simulations are generated using the state-of-the-art AxiSEM3D simulator, which ensures high fidelity and quality of the data.
* A comprehensive set of representative ML-based PDE solvers are benchmarked, providing valuable insights into their relative performance on this new task.
* The work demonstrates high reproducibility and clarity, with the code and dataset being made fully public. The presentation is clear, with well-structured diagrams and tables.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
- The paper lacks benchmarks for the most complex 'Real Earth' tier. While the Acoustic and Elastic tiers are thoroughly evaluated, the absence of results for this key component makes it difficult to assess the practical utility of the framework for real-world applications.
- While the paper contrasts the high speed of ML models with a single, high-fidelity numerical simulation, it lacks a broader discussion on the speed-accuracy trade-off within traditional numerical methods themselves (e.g., comparing simulations with different mesh resolutions). 
- As the authors acknowledge in Section 3.2.3, a significant gap exists between the synthetic data and real-world observations, making its applicability to real-world scenarios uncertain.
- The analysis of the benchmark results lacks spatially resolved evaluation. While global performance metrics are provided, a more localized error analysis (e.g., by geographic region) would offer deeper insights into the model's performance characteristics.

ethical_considerations.value: No, there are no or only very minor ethics concerns

dataset_code_comments.value:
The authors provide clear and direct links to all assets. The dataset is provided in the HDF5 format, a standard format for large-scale scientific data. The work is exceptionally well-documented, with detailed appendices covering:

- The physical constraints and equations used (Appendix B).
- Detailed configurations for each dataset tier (Appendix C).
- Hyperparameters and implementation details for all baseline models (Appendix F). 

The combination of publicly available code, the accessible dataset, and meticulous documentation provides all the necessary components to fully support reproducibility.

additional_feedback.value:
Questions

* Regarding reproducibility, does the public repository include the specific code or commands used for generating the datasets with AxiSEM3D?
* How robust is the InversionMLP model to noise in the input seismograms? Since real-world data is inherently noisy, understanding the model's stability is crucial for its practical utility.
* What is the definition of the colon notation used in the Eq. (A3)? double dot product? For clarity, it would be beneficial for the authors to briefly define the notation.

final_justification.value:
* In their rebuttal, the authors provided clear and detailed responses to the concerns I raised, including the lack of benchmarking on the Real Earth tier, the absence of a quantitative discussion on the speed-accuracy trade-off, and the need for spatially resolved performance analysis.

* Regarding the Real Earth tier, the authors clarified that benchmarking is currently ongoing and will be released soon, indicating the continued development and scalability of the work.

* They also presented quantitative robustness experiments showing the model's resilience to input noise and missing data, which strengthens the practical relevance of the dataset and models.

* Additionally, the newly provided latitude-based performance analysis revealed performance degradation in polar regions, along with plausible causes and plans for improvement.

* Based on these clarifications, I consider that all my initial concerns have been sufficiently addressed. The paper presents a high-quality dataset and a comprehensive benchmark, representing a valuable contribution to the ML-for-geophysics community.

Final Recommendation: 5 (Accept)

title.value: GlobalTomo: A global dataset for physics-ML seismic wavefield modeling and FWI

abstract.value: Global seismic tomography, taking advantage of seismic waves from natural earthquakes, provides essential insights into the earth's internal dynamics. Advanced Full-Waveform Inversion (FWI) techniques, whose aim is to meticulously interpret every detail in seismograms, confront formidable computational demands in forward modeling and adjoint simulations on a global scale. Recent advancements in Machine Learning (ML) offer a transformative potential for accelerating the computational efficiency of FWI and extending its applicability to larger scales. This work presents the first 3D global synthetic dataset tailored for seismic wavefield modeling and full-waveform tomography, referred to as the Global Tomography (GlobalTomo) dataset. This dataset is comprehensive, incorporating explicit wave physics and robust geophysical parameterization at realistic global scales, generated through state-of-the-art forward simulations optimized for 3D global wavefield calculations. Through extensive analysis and the establishment of ML baselines, we illustrate that ML approaches are particularly suitable for global FWI, overcoming its limitations with rapid forward modeling and flexible inversion strategies. This work represents a cross-disciplinary effort to enhance our understanding of the earth's interior through physics-ML modeling.
